claims.text: Flash-SPS of submicron ZrB2 at 1650–1700 °C can produce fully dense, single-phase ZrB2.
The proposed flash-SPS ZrB2 will have superior mechanical integrity to conventionally processed high-temperature ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature ZrB2.
The proposed flash-SPS ZrB2 will have superior oxidation resistance to conventionally processed high-temperature ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature ZrB2.
The proposed flash-SPS ZrB2 will have superior liquid-metal corrosion resistance to conventionally processed high-temperature ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature ZrB2.
The intended precursor is submicron, secondary-phase-free, undoped ZrB2 powder.
A heating rate of at least 200 °C/min, a 5–10 minute dwell, and a pressure of approximately 50–60 MPa are applicable parameters for densifying ZrB2 at 1650–1700 °C.
Vacuum or argon will avoid oxidation during the proposed sintering cycle.
Field assistance and rapid heating will cause substantial densification.
A short dwell will minimize grain growth in ZrB2.
Rapid, pressure-assisted mass transport in flash-SPS will eliminate pores in ZrB2.
Flash-SPS will reduce oxide inclusions or intergranular secondary phases in ZrB2.
Porosity and oxide inclusions adversely affect mechanical and oxidation performance.
A dense, fine-grained ZrB2 matrix will improve the protective surface layer formed during oxidation or liquid-metal exposure.
The proposed process will yield higher density and flexural strength than ZrB2 processed above 2300 °C and prior sub-1800 °C specimens.
The proposed material will be suitable for extended high-temperature service in oxidizing and liquid-plating-metal environments.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires approximately 2300 °C sintering.
Earlier lower-temperature ZrB2 processes produced insufficient density or poor oxidation or corrosion performance.
Submicron starting powder is required for the proposed low-temperature densification mechanism.
Residual oxide contamination, nonuniform densification, defects, or second phases would reduce oxidation and corrosion performance.
Scale-up may impair density uniformity and mechanical properties.
